topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
usual_baseline: Request-to-scan often meets targets, but presentation-to-MRI is long: mean 12.5 hours [1646], median 5.9 hours [1687], 438 minutes [1318]. Only 15% referred with an MRI done [1279]. CES confirmed in only 7–18% of referrals or scans. Documentation of perianal sensation 72% and spinal plan 20% [1607].
fix_that_works: An orthopaedic middle grade in ED: mean MRI wait 12.5 to 8 hours, same-day discharge 29% to 58% [1646]. Referral 176 to 60.8 minutes, MRI 438 to 185 minutes [1318]. Teaching and SBAR template: perianal sensation 72% to 97% [1607]. SOP and triage work: unnecessary MRIs 38% to 18% [1687].
fix_that_fails: Three PDSA cycles left median presentation-to-MRI at 5.7 hours; scanners closing at 20:00 blocked it [1687]. Senior ED discussion fell 61.9% to 9% and documented spinal plan 20% to 0% [1607].
consultant_advice: Time to MRI depends on scanner hours and staffing more than on trainees. Audit the whole pathway from arrival, not just request-to-scan, which usually passes. The yield of scans and discharge safety are more useful than another timing audit.
